summary: Elevated TTFB on chat completions after model/runtime upgrades
description: Customers (notably Acme Analytics) are reporting elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) on chat completion streaming responses after recent runtime and model upgrades (runtime v1.4.5 + model redwood-chat-3.2). Impact: increased frontend latencies, client timeouts (~5-10% of requests), and degraded UX for streaming chat. Issue began immediately after a staged rollout on 2026-03-03. This ticket tracks triage, investigation, customer communication, and remediation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Make a chat completion request (streaming=true) against /v1/chat/completions using model=redwood-chat-3.2 in prod-us-east
2) Observe server TTFB metric reported in tracing/span start -> first token emitted
3) Compare to baseline (pre-upgrade) where p50 TTFB ~ 60ms; current observed p50 ~ 300-450ms and p95 up to 1.2s
4) Optionally pin runtime to v1.4.4 or model to redwood-chat-3.1 to reproduce difference
logs: 2026-03-03T14:12:03Z TRACE request-id=6f2a1e span=streaming/handler TTFB=430ms model=redwood-chat-3.2 runtime=v1.4.5
2026-03-03T14:15:10Z ERROR request-id=7b9cfd timeout at client-side after 1.0s waiting for first token
Aggregated metrics (prod-us-east, 2026-03-03 13:00-15:00): p50 TTFB increased from 62ms -> 378ms, error-rate (client timeouts) increased from 0.2% -> 4.8%
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: model change (redwood-chat-3.2) introduced heavier cold-start or longer first-token kernel path
Observed correlation with runtime upgrade v1.4.5 (deployed 2026-03-03 12:40 UTC) — timeframe matches customer reports
Tracing shows increased time in kernel selection and first-token generation path (span 'kernel/select' and 'kv/cache-warm')
KV cache warm-up latency increased for streamed requests; prefix caching appears not to be used for some requests due to minor hash schema mismatch introduced in model-registry PR #129
Reproduced in canary: pinning runtime to v1.4.4 drops TTFB back to baseline; pinning model to redwood-chat-3.1 also drops TTFB — suggests combined effect
No evidence of infrastructure-level resource exhaustion (GPU utilization normal, no OOMs), but increased CPU time in runtime workers during first-token for streaming requests
Related internal ticket INT-4121 records a kernel scheduling optimization in runtime v1.4.5 that changed selection ordering under certain sequence-length profiles

root_cause: Interaction between runtime kernel selection changes introduced in runtime v1.4.5 and a model registry metadata change for redwood-chat-3.2 caused certain streaming chat requests to take a slower kernel/codepath for first-token generation. The slow path increased TTFB for affected requests.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: customer pinned to runtime v1.4.4 via routing rule and we offered model pinning to redwood-chat-3.1. Engineering merged a rollback/patch PR (runtime PR #847) to revert the kernel selection behavior and added a guard for KV-layout compatibility. Patch scheduled for staged deploy 2026-03-04 02:00 UTC. Post-deploy verification checklist created.
follow_up_actions: 1) Deploy runtime patch (PR #847) to prod via staged rollout and monitor TTFB metrics closely
2) Add automated compatibility check in model-registry pipeline to detect KV-layout changes that could affect runtime selection
3) Improve canary coverage for streaming-first-token latency during runtime/model upgrades
4) Create runbook for rapid rollback/pinning for future runtime-model compatibility regressions (Confluence ID: runbooks/ttfb-investigation)
5) Communicate postmortem to impacted customers and update status page if material
